messages.subject: Actical Z MiniMitter
parts:
Hello, 

I am very new to physical activity monitoring and need to analyse some data collected using Actical Z MiniMitter. Is GGIR able to analyse this data? 

The file extensions is .AWCF but I can download the raw data into a csv and it is outputted as activity counts per 60second epoch.  
I have seen the read.myacc.csv
but I was unsure what unit to use. Any assistance would be appreciated.

messages.subject: Re: Actical Z MiniMitter
parts:
Hi Danielle, I have a similar problem which I'm still trying to resolve. In my case, I want to run GGIR on a csv file also cointaining activity counts per epoch. These were derived from raw acceleration values elsewhere, but I want to analyze the activity time series in order to compare the results with those from other activity count files from another device.
I believe the read.myacc.csv function works for csv containing accelerometric data. But given that GGIR can process activity counts time series (Actiwatch csv, for example), it shouldn't be impossible to make it work. 
Right now, I'm formatting my data so it looks like an Actiwatch file to see if it works.
Hopefully someone else whill chime in with more info.

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Actical Z MiniMitter
parts:
Hello both,

read.myacc.csv is intended for raw data (many values per second) as explained in the documentation.

GGIR facilitates externally derived count data for some data formats such as Actiwatch csv and awd files. If you want it to also work with Actical data than please help either by dedicating time to enhance the GGIR code or help by finding funding for someone such as me to do the work.

Thanks,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/
